R: Across all functions, whenever a numeric argument is NULL, a boolean, non-numeric text, or not finite (NaN or infinity), treat it as 0; numeric text such as '12' is read as that number.
Across all functions, whenever a date argument is NULL, not a string, or not a real calendar date in the exact form YYYY-MM-DD (surrounding spaces are ignored), treat it as 1970-01-01.
Across all functions, whenever a text argument is NULL, treat it as empty text; a non-text value is treated as its printed text.
Whenever a function adds months to a date and the target month lacks that day, the result spills into the following month by the missing days (e.g. 31 Jan plus 1 month is 2 or 3 March).
Whenever a date calculation goes beyond the supported calendar (year over 9999), the function returns NULL.
Whenever a money result is computed, round it up (never down) to the next whole cent and return it as a number.
Whenever a text result is longer than 12 characters, cut it to its first 12 characters.
Whenever dose_mg gets a negative weight or a negative mg_per_kg, treat that value as 0.
Whenever dose_mg computes weight times mg_per_kg, round the product up to a whole mg.
Whenever dose_mg's rounded dose exceeds 500, return 500; the result is always a whole number from 0 to 500.
Whenever visit_fee gets minutes of 0 or less (including NULL or unreadable), return 0 with no minimum fee, whatever the rate.
Whenever visit_fee has minutes above 0, bill time in 15-minute blocks and round partial blocks up to a whole block.
Whenever visit_fee has minutes above 0, the fee is blocks times hourly_rate divided by 4.
Whenever visit_fee has minutes above 0 and the fee is under 30 (including a zero, negative or missing rate), charge the minimum fee of 30.
Whenever size_class gets a weight of 1 kg or less (including 0, negative, NULL or unreadable), return 'micro'.
Whenever size_class gets a weight above 1 and up to and including 6 kg, return 'small'.
Whenever size_class gets a weight above 6 and up to and including 25 kg, return 'medium'.
Whenever size_class gets a weight above 25 and up to and including 45 kg, return 'large'.
Whenever size_class gets a weight above 45 kg, return 'giant'.
Whenever vaccine_next_due gets an interval, drop its fractional part toward zero before use.
Whenever vaccine_next_due gets an interval of 0 or less after that (including NULL or unreadable), use 12 months instead.
Whenever vaccine_next_due is computed, add the interval in months to last_date with no weekday adjustment.
Whenever pet_tag builds either part, keep only the ASCII letters and digits of the name or surname, drop everything else (spaces, punctuation, accents), and upper-case them.
Whenever a pet_tag part is empty after cleaning (blank, NULL or only symbols), use 'STRAY' for that part.
Whenever pet_tag assembles its result, write the pet part, a hyphen, then the surname part, and cut to 12 characters.
Whenever boarding_cost gets days of 0 or less (including NULL or unreadable), return 0 whatever the rate.
Whenever boarding_cost gets a negative daily_rate, treat the rate as 0.
Whenever boarding_cost gets a fractional number of days, round the days up to a whole day.
Whenever boarding_cost charges days, charge the first 7 days at the full daily_rate.
Whenever boarding_cost charges days beyond the 7th, charge each at 80 percent of the daily_rate.
Whenever loyalty_tier gets visits, drop the fractional part downward, treat negatives as 0, and count at most 30 visits.
Whenever loyalty_tier gets a negative total_spent, treat it as 0.
Whenever loyalty_tier scores a client, the score is 10 points per counted visit plus 1 point per whole 10 of total_spent (fraction dropped).
Whenever loyalty_tier has a score of 100 or less, return 'bronze'.
Whenever loyalty_tier has a score above 100 and up to and including 300, return 'silver'.
Whenever loyalty_tier has a score above 300 and up to and including 600, return 'gold'.
Whenever loyalty_tier has a score above 600, return 'platinum'.
Whenever membership_expiry gets months, drop the fractional part toward zero, treat negatives as 0, and limit it to at most 60.
Whenever membership_expiry adds the months to start_date, a month of 0 gives the start date itself.
Whenever membership_expiry lands on a Sunday (after any month-end spill), move the expiry to the following Monday; other weekdays and Saturdays are unchanged.
Whenever adoption_anniversary gets years, round to the nearest whole year with halves rounding up (2.5 becomes 3).
Whenever adoption_anniversary's rounded years are negative, return NULL.
Whenever adoption_anniversary has rounded years of 0 (including NULL or unreadable years), return the adoption date itself.
Whenever adoption_anniversary adds years, it adds 12 months per year, so 29 February in a non-leap target year becomes 1 March, and there is no weekday adjustment.
Whenever owner_label gets names, trim spaces around both names first.
Whenever owner_label has a non-blank last name, show it with only its first letter upper-case and all other letters lower-case (so 'McDONALD' becomes 'Mcdonald').
Whenever owner_label has a blank or NULL last name, use 'Unknown' as the surname.
Whenever owner_label has a non-blank first name, print the surname, a comma and a space, the upper-cased first character of the first name, and a full stop.
Whenever owner_label has a blank or NULL first name, print the surname alone with no comma or initial.
Whenever owner_label's result is longer than 12 characters, cut it to 12 characters.
Whenever late_fee gets days_late of 5 or fewer (including NULL or unreadable), return 0; days_late is not rounded, so 5.5 days is already late.
Whenever late_fee gets an invoice_amount of 0 or less (including NULL or unreadable), return 0.
Whenever late_fee applies, the fee is 0.5 percent of invoice_amount for each day late.
Whenever late_fee's computed fee exceeds 25 percent of invoice_amount, charge 25 percent of invoice_amount instead.
Whenever insurance_payout gets a negative deductible, treat it as 0.
Whenever insurance_payout computes the reimbursable part, subtract the deductible from the claim_amount and never go below 0.
Whenever insurance_payout has a claim_amount of 1000 or less, reimburse 80 percent of the reimbursable part.
Whenever insurance_payout has a claim_amount above 1000, reimburse 50 percent of the reimbursable part; the rate is chosen by the claim before the deductible, so the whole claim drops to 50 percent.
Whenever insurance_payout gets a zero, negative, NULL or unreadable claim_amount, return 0.
Whenever installment_date gets an installment_no, drop its fractional part downward and limit it to between 1 and 12, so anything below 1 counts as 1 and anything above 12 counts as 12.
Whenever installment_date computes the date, add (installment_no minus 1) months to first_due_date, so instalment 1 is the first due date itself, with no weekday adjustment.
Whenever invoice_code builds the prefix, keep only the ASCII letters of the prefix, upper-case them, and use the first 3.
Whenever invoice_code has fewer than 3 prefix letters (including none, NULL or digits only), pad the prefix on the right with 'X' to 3 letters.
Whenever invoice_code gets a year, drop its fractional part downward and print only its last two digits, zero-padded to two (2005 gives '05'; NULL or unreadable gives '00').

Whenever invoice_code gets a number, drop its fractional part downward, treat negatives as 0, and print it with at least 4 digits, zero-padded on the left; longer numbers are not shortened except by the 12-character cut.
Whenever invoice_code assembles its result, write prefix, two-digit year, a hyphen, then the number, and cut to 12 characters.
Whenever reminder_text gets days_until, drop its fractional part downward (NULL or unreadable counts as 0).
Whenever reminder_text has days_until below 0, the message ending is 'overdue'.
Whenever reminder_text has days_until of 0, the message ending is 'today'.
Whenever reminder_text has days_until of 1, the message ending is 'tomorrow'.
Whenever reminder_text has days_until of 2 or more, the message ending is 'in Nd' where N is the whole number of days (e.g. 'in 14d').
Whenever reminder_text assembles its message, trim the pet name, write the name, a space, then the ending, and cut to 12 characters, so a long name can cut the ending short.
Whenever reminder_text has a blank or NULL pet name, the message is just the ending with no leading space.
